summary.text: A plate boundary is where two of Earth's tectonic plates meet, and their relative motion there makes it convergent, divergent or transform.
At convergent boundaries one plate is carried down into the mantle, while at divergent ones seafloor spreading makes new crust, keeping Earth's surface area constant.
Plate boundaries are where earthquakes strike and where mountains, volcanoes, mid-ocean ridges and oceanic trenches form.

facts.label: Most active volcano belt
facts.value: The Pacific plate's Ring of Fire

facts.label: Ocean lithosphere thickness
facts.value: About 6 km at ridges, over 100 km at subduction zones

items.prompt: At one boundary, the edge of a plate is carried down under its neighbour into the mantle. What type of boundary is it?
items.explain: Subduction, one plate going down under another, happens along convergent boundaries.

items.prompt: New ocean crust forms at spreading ridges all the time, yet Earth's surface area stays the same. Why?

options.label: New crust shrinks as it cools down
The planet slowly swells to make room
Crust is lost where plates sink under others
Ridges only make crust every few million years

items.explain: Subduction at convergent boundaries removes surface, balancing the new crust made by seafloor spreading in a kind of conveyor belt.

items.prompt: Where do the vast majority of the world's active volcanoes sit?

options.label: Spread fairly evenly across the globe
Mostly near the North and South Poles
Along the edges where plates meet

items.explain: Most active volcanoes lie along plate boundaries; only some occur in plate interiors.

items.prompt: Oceanic lithosphere forms at a mid-ocean ridge and moves away from it. Where is it thinnest?
items.explain: It cools and thickens with age as it moves away, from about 6 km at the ridge to over 100 km at subduction zones.

items.prompt: Plates at the Mid-Atlantic Ridge move apart at about the speed at which what grows?
items.explain: Motion there is 10 to 40 millimetres a year, about as fast as fingernails grow.

items.prompt: Where an ocean plate meets a continental plate, which one usually sinks into the mantle?
items.explain: Oceanic crust is denser than continental crust, and cold, dense oceanic crust is what sinks into the mantle at subduction zones.
